passage:
The old fire station was turned into a children's safety museum. The red doors remained, and an old fire truck stood inside.
Children learned how firefighters worked in the past and how fire safety rules had changed. They practiced crawling under smoke, checking door heat, and calling emergency services.
A retired firefighter told them that courage was important, but preparation saved more lives.
The building had once sent help into the city. Now it taught people how to avoid needing help.
The fire station's purpose changed, but its spirit stayed close to safety. Some buildings can retire from one job and begin another.
